pageCache.text:
Young Women's Hub
We are an independent school that provides a safe and nurturing environment in which young women can thrive
Educate Nurture Inspire
Welcome to The Young Women's Hub
Home
Welcome to The Young Women’s Hub, an independent school and registered charity dedicated to supporting young women aged 11-19 to become confident, capable, and future-ready, regardless of any obstacles they have faced so far. Our mission is to empower every student through a calm, structured learning environment using individual learning passports that value wellbeing alongside academic progress.
We believe that education should equip each young woman with both knowledge and self-belief. Alongside strong teaching which understands students' needs and clear expectations, our pastoral approach helps students build resilience, develop positive relationships, and gain the skills they need to thrive at school and beyond.
Our holistic and nurturing approach brings together academic support, wellbeing guidance, and practical life skills. For parents, we offer clear communication and a partnership mindset—so you can feel confident that your daughter is supported, challenged, and encouraged every step of the way.
View the latest updates on our calendar.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Vision, Mission and values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision, Mission Statement and Our Values
Vision
The Young Women’s Hub vision is dedicated to create a supportive and nurturing environment for young women who face challenges in accessing mainstream education. Our focus is on providing tailored educational programs and life skills that empower these young women to build confidence and self-belief. By equipping them with the tools they need to succeed, we aim to help them thrive and achieve their goals, regardless of their circumstances or backgrounds.
Mission Statement
Our mission is to empower and inspire vulnerable young women through a holistic approach that includes education, social awareness, mentoring, and nurturing support. We strive to create a transformative environment where these young women can develop their potential, gain confidence, and become active, informed members of their communities.
Our Values
Nurture
We are committed to nurturing and supporting vulnerable young women within the local community. We provide holistic, wraparound care in a safe and calming environment, focusing on fostering each student's individual strengths and talents. The Young Women’s Hub offers a unique educational experience that extends beyond the traditional classroom, integrating various support services to address the diverse needs of our students. Our goal is to help these young women grow into confident, successful individuals ready to thrive in the future.
Inspire
We aim to inspire and motivate vulnerable young women by connecting them with positive female role models and mentors. These relationships provide essential support, guiding them to develop resilience, confidence, and the skills needed to become successful women in the future. Our commitment is to empower each young woman to reach her full potential and navigate life's challenges with strength and determination.
Educate
We aim to educate and inspire young women by offering a blend of vocational and formal educational options. We provide a supportive environment where students can explore their passions and develop their skills through discovery and personal growth. We believe in empowering young women to reach their full potential, equipping them for a successful future. Our commitment is to foster a love of learning and a sense of confidence that will serve them throughout their lives.
Celebrating Diversity
Our mission is to champion diversity and empower young women to overcome oppression and challenges. We strive to create a supportive, inclusive environment where every young woman can thrive and reach her full potential. We believe that education and mentorship are powerful tools that equip young women to navigate the complexities of the world, fostering resilience and confidence for a brighter future.
Striving for Excellence
Our young women deserve the best academic and personal support. As a school, we are committed to continuously developing and improving our services by engaging with external providers and actively involving our students in this process. We believe that collaboration and feedback from our students are essential in creating a nurturing environment that meets their unique needs and helps them succeed.
Developing Partnerships
We actively seek opportunities to collaborate with relevant organizations and agencies to enhance life outcomes for young women. By forging partnerships, we aim to provide comprehensive support and resources that empower our students to thrive in all aspects of their lives. Together, we can create meaningful pathways for growth, opportunity, and success.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Post-16 education for young people with SEND
pageCache.text:
Post‑16 Education information for Young People and their families with SEND
Leaving school at 16 can feel like a big step, but it also brings new opportunities, independence and the chance to shape your future. If you are unsure about your next move, every school has a designated staff member who can support you with careers guidance and help you explore your options.
Lewisham’s full Post‑16 SEND information is available here:
👉 Post‑16 education for young people with SEND https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/send/post-16-education-for-young-people-with-send (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
All young people must remain in education or training until their 18th birthday. This does not mean you must stay at school — several pathways may suit your interests, learning style, and support needs.
You can stay at your current school or apply to a different sixth form if they offer the subjects or vocational courses you want. Visiting open days and exploring websites can help you decide.
Find sixth form options in Lewisham: 👉 Sixth form colleges in Lewisham https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/schools/sixth-form-colleges (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
Many special schools also offer post‑16 pathways.
Further education colleges offer a wide range of courses for all abilities, including supported learning programmes for young people aged 16–25 with SEND. These may include:
IT and business skills
Pathways to independence
Catering and horticulture
Preparation for employment
More information: 👉 Further education options for over 16s https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/send/post-16-education-for-young-people-with-send/further-education-options-for-over-16s (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
Apprenticeships allow you to:
Gain real work experience
Achieve a nationally recognised qualification
Apprenticeships exist in many fields, including engineering, accountancy, financial services, digital roles and veterinary nursing.
Useful links: 👉 National Apprenticeship Service https://www.apprenticeships.gov.uk/ (apprenticeships.gov.uk in Bing) 👉 Lewisham Apprenticeship Programme https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/post-16-education-and-training/apprenticeships (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
Traineeships are designed for young people who need additional support before progressing to an apprenticeship or employment. They include:
English and maths (if needed)
Work preparation training
High‑quality work experience
Programmes last from six weeks to six months, with up to 80% of learning taking place in a workplace.
More information: 👉 NEET Traineeship https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/post-16-education-and-training/traineeships (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
Supported internships help young people with higher or complex needs gain meaningful work experience with tailored support. You must have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or a Learning Disability Assessment to apply.
Lewisham’s supported internship information: 👉 Supported internships and opportunities https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/send/post-16-education-for-young-people-with-send/supported-internships (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)
Additional resources: 👉 Preparing for Adulthood – Supported Internships https://www.preparingforadulthood.org.uk/what-we-do/supported-internships (preparingforadulthood.org.uk in Bing)
This includes videos, accessible fact sheets and stories from young people who have completed internships.
If you continue your studies and achieve a Level 3 qualification (A‑levels, BTECs or equivalent), higher education may be an option.
More information: 👉 Higher education options for over 16s https://lewisham.gov.uk/myservices/education/send/post-16-education-for-young-people-with-send/higher-education-options-for-over-16s (lewisham.gov.uk in Bing)

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Corporate Partnerships
pageCache.text:
Corporate Partnerships
The Young Women’s Hub welcomes enquiries from strong corporate partnerships to help SEND students and other young people access inspiring learning opportunities. Through carefully planned projects, businesses can support workshops, mentoring, and real-world experiences that help students build confidence, skills, and ambition for their next steps.
We work with partners who value inclusion and want to make a measurable difference. Whether you can offer work experience, career talks, volunteering, or resources, we match support to what schools and students need most. Our approach is versatile, allowing partnerships to be tailored to different year groups and learning goals, including additional support for SEND students.
Partnering with The Young Women’s Hub also strengthens your organisation’s community impact. Together, we create positive pathways into education, training, and future careers, helping young people feel supported and motivated. If you’re interested in working with us, we can discuss partnership ideas and agree on clear outcomes that benefit students and your team.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Parent and Carers
pageCache.text:
Parent and Carers
We understand that choosing the right school for your daughter is a big decision - especially when she's been through challenges in education. At The Young Women's Hub, we're here to support you every step of the way, with the communication and care you deserve.
We're not just a school - we're a nurturing environment where young women can rebuild their confidence, reconnect with learning, and take positive steps toward a brighter future.
How We Support Your Child
At YWH, we take a personalised, whole-child approach. That means:
Our goal is to help your child feel safe, heard, and understood - and to make sure she knows where she belongs.
Working in Partnership With You
We believe you are the expert on your child, and your insight is key to her success.
We're here to listen. If you're worried about anything, you can talk to us. No judgement - just a commitment to support your child in the best way we can.
The Referral Process
If your daughter is not currently attending YWH and you think our school could be the right place for her, we encourage you to speak with her current school, caseworker or local authority. Professionals can refer directly through our Referral Form, and we're always happy to answer questions before that step.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Safeguarding Young People
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding Young People
CEOP is here to keep children safe from sexual abuse and grooming online. You can make a report directly to the CEOP Safety Centre by clicking on the Click CEOP button below, If something has happened online which has made you feel unsafe, scared or worried, from from someone you know in real life, or someone you have only met online.
CEOP take all reports seriously and we will do everything we can to keep you safe. As well as making a report to the CEOP Safety Centre, the CEOP Education website has information and advice to help you if something has happened to you online.
Are you being bullied?
CEOP are unable to respond to reports about bullying but if you’re being bullied and would like to talk to someone in confidence right now you can speak to Childline on 0800 1111 or talk to them online – no worry is too big or too small.

🌼 The Young Women’s Hub
A specialist SEND school community for young women
The Young Women’s Hub is a specialist school community providing a safe, supportive, and empowering environment for secondary‑aged young women. We deliver high‑quality SEND education, personalised learning programmes, and targeted wellbeing support to help every student thrive academically, socially, and emotionally.
Personalised learning and therapeutic support
Our curriculum blends academic study with individual learning plans, additional therapies, and structured mentoring sessions. Each young woman receives tailored support designed to build confidence, strengthen resilience, and re‑engage positively with education. We focus on practical skills, emotional wellbeing, and preparation for future education, training, and employment.
Working together for the right support
We collaborate closely with professional referrals, local agencies, and families to ensure every student receives the right help at the right time. Our team coordinates support pathways, shares information appropriately, and guides families through the SEND options available locally.
A safe, nurturing place to grow
Our aim is to provide clear, consistent support for wellbeing, learning needs, and everyday challenges. Through mentoring, therapeutic interventions, and personalised activities, we help young women feel heard, valued, and equipped to take positive steps forward.
The Young Women’s Hub is a place where young women can learn, grow, and build a future with confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - Young Women's Hub Curriculum offer
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Intent and Implementation at The Young Women’s Hub
The Young Women’s Hub offers an ambitious, inclusive curriculum that is designed to secure strong progress and positive outcomes for all learners. We aim to ensure every student develops a secure understanding of core concepts while mastering key skills across a wide range of academic and vocational subjects. Our curriculum is carefully sequenced and delivered in a way that allows students to build on prior learning and deepen their knowledge over time.
Developing Key Skills for Life and Work
We prioritise essential skills such as literacy (including guided reading), numeracy, digital competency, communication skills, personal resilience, and critical thinking. These form the foundation of both academic achievement and personal development, equipping students for future education, employment, and independent living.
Adaptive Learning and Personalised Support
Teaching is tailored to meet individual student needs through adaptive teaching strategies, including personalised e-learning platforms such as Sparx Maths. Regular assessment helps staff identify knowledge gaps, adapt delivery, and provide targeted interventions, ensuring every student can access the curriculum and make sustained progress.
Individual Timetables and Learner-Led Pathways
Each student follows a bespoke timetable designed around their starting points, interests, and aspirations. This personalised approach supports engagement and motivation, giving students ownership over their educational journey. Vocational courses are offered alongside core subjects to nurture practical strengths and prepare students for real-world opportunities.
Monitoring Impact and Holistic Growth
Student progress is closely tracked using formative and summative assessment. We also assess life skills and emotional wellbeing at key points in each placement, recognising the importance of holistic development. Staff monitor qualitative outcomes to ensure students not only thrive academically but also develop confidence, self-awareness, and ambition through mentoring and small group work.
Curriculum Impact and Future Readiness
Our curriculum ensures students leave The Young Women’s Hub with the knowledge, skills, and personal development needed to succeed in the next stage of their education. We foster a culture of high expectations, personalised challenge, and inclusive opportunity that empowers young women to take ownership of their progress and plan for a successful future.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - SEND Offering
pageCache.text:
SEND Educational Placements
Welcome to the Young Women’s Hub, where we are committed to supporting every student's educational journey. For parents of secondary age children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), we provide a tailored approach through our SEND offer. Our goal is to ensure that every student receives the support they require to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally.
At the core of our SEND provision is the development of Individual Passports. These passports are bespoke education plans that are created to address the specific needs of each individual student. By collaborating closely with parents, carers, Teachers, the Senco and support staff, we ensure that these passports are holistic, covering not only academic goals but also emotional and social needs. This personalised approach helps us to empower our students, fostering independence and confidence in their abilities.
Furthermore, the implementation of Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCP) is a critical component of our SEND framework. These plans are designed to provide a comprehensive and cohesive approach to education and healthcare, ensuring that all necessary support is given to facilitate the optimal development of our students.
At the Young Women’s Hub, we are dedicated to working alongside parents/carers and professionals to deliver a holistic educational experience that meets the unique needs of each student.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Young Women's Hub - SEND Support
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Support
At The Young Women's Hub, we are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive environment for our students - especially those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
We understand that many of the young women who join us may have complex learning needs, social, emotional, or mental health challenges, or existing Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs).
Our approach is centred around early identification, individualised planning and learning passports, and collaborative working - always involving the young person, their family, and any professionals already supporting them.
Every learner at YWH receives personalised support tailored to her strengths, needs and aspirations. Whether she requires in-class adjustments, targeted interventions, or therapeutic input, we're here to help her feel safe, make progress, and succeed in all areas of her development.
